text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.23% today to $137.35, capping a solid 6% two-week gain as oil prices remain elevated above $97 per barrel domestically and $109.50 globally. The stock's steady climb reflects sustained strength in crude markets, which have been driven by Middle East tensions—Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West pipeline after drone attacks from Iran-allied forces this week, combined with ongoing geopolitical friction between the U.S. and Iran, has kept prices well above $100 a barrel despite brief retreats on hopes of diplomatic progress.

The near-term uncertainty about whether Middle East tensions will ease or escalate is creating the volatility we're seeing in both oil and oil majors' stocks. While Trump has suggested Iran conflict could end post-election and lead to lower prices, Iran's leadership has rejected surrender, and the physical damage to Saudi infrastructure remains real—so markets are staying cautious and keeping crude prices elevated for now.
